Class OutputLock

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.dev.compile.OutputLock
@Internal public final class OutputLock extends Object
The lock of a project's class outputs, shared by every development process of the project: development mode and test mode run at once, as mnDev beside mnTest, both compile the application's sources into the same output, with the same staging, backup and mapping files beside it, and each snapshots what the other writes. A compilation, from reading the output's state to promoting what it produced, holds the lock, and so does every read of the outputs as a whole, a generation's snapshot or the digest of what changed: neither process sees the other's compilation half done.

Between processes it is a file lock on a file beside the output; within one it is a reentrant lock, since the JVM holds a file lock for the process and not for a thread. The file lock is taken by the outermost hold and released with it. A build's clean deletes the lock file and another process creates it again, so once the file lock is taken the path must still name the locked file, or the file the path names now is locked instead.
